你好，Deck of Souls游戏开发者，我是一名中国玩家，也是一位忠实的卡牌游戏爱好者，在游玩过Deck of Souls后非常喜欢这款游戏，但也有非常多的遗憾，希望可以以这种方式帮助游戏做的更好。 首先我在游玩的过程中遇到了很多BUG，比如毒药卡牌的描述是在敌方回合开始前生效，但是实际效果是在敌方回合结束生效，很显然回合开始时生效是比较合理的。另一个BUG也是关于毒药卡牌的，描述里是每回合-1毒药，实际上是每回合+1，这显然是个不合理的BUG。 另外一点我想提的建议也许有些刻薄，sorry，我觉得游戏里每一个BOSS都是双BOSS的设定非常愚蠢，或许可以把双BOSS的设定变化为增加1个或2个精英，在最终BOSS时再设计为双BOSS（参考Slay the Spire进阶20）。 其它的一些问题就是关于数值的问题，我知道数值是卡牌游戏的核心，这很难设计，但是目前Deck of Souls还是有数值不合理的地方，比如角色太过于强大缺少挑战的感觉，还有就是关于成长曲线的问题。 关于三位游戏角色，我个人认为法师是最强的，其次是战士，猎人或许有些弱了？也许毒药卡牌的BUG可以修复好或许可以改变我的想法，另外让我想不通的是，为什么一个职业的卡牌选择除了中立卡牌会有其它职业的卡牌？难道开发者不觉得这么设计会导致非常混乱吗？或许这里也可以修复一下。 抱歉说了一些刻薄的话，但是我真的非常喜欢这款游戏，希望它可以变得更好。我是一名卡牌游戏的老玩家，从小除了中国本土的卡牌游戏，也游玩了Slay the Spire、Duel Monsters、HearthStone、Gwent、Magic The Gathering等等，这些年也没有让人眼前一亮的作品，直到Deck of Souls的出现，它不够完美，但是非常有潜力，非常希望可以通过修复优化和调整让这款游戏变得优秀起来，甚至可以媲美明年要发行的Slay the Spire2，我真的非常喜欢Deck of Souls这款游戏，希望自己想要传达的可以表达清楚。 【英文原文（机器翻译）】 【Original English (machine translation)】 Hello, Deck of Souls game developer, I am a Chinese player and a loyal card game enthusiast. After playing Deck of Souls, I like this game very much, but I also have many regrets. I hope to help make the game better in this way. First of all, I encountered many bugs during the game. For example, the description of the poison card is that it takes effect before the enemy's turn begins, but the actual effect takes effect at the end of the enemy's turn. Obviously, it is more reasonable to take effect at the beginning of the turn. Another bug is also about the poison card. The description says -1 poison per turn, but it is actually +1 per turn. This is obviously an unreasonable bug. Another suggestion I want to make may be a bit harsh, sorry, I think it is very stupid to set every BOSS in the game as a double BOSS. Maybe the setting of double BOSS can be changed to add 1 or 2 elites, and then design it as a double BOSS at the final BOSS (refer to Slay the Spire Advanced 20). Some other issues are about numbers. I know that numbers are the core of card games, which is difficult to design, but there are still unreasonable numbers in Deck of Souls, such as the characters are too powerful and lack a sense of challenge, and there are also problems with the growth curve. Regarding the three game characters, I personally think that the mage is the strongest, followed by the warrior, and the hunter may be a little weak? Maybe the bug of the poison card can be fixed and may change my mind. What I can't figure out is why a class's card selection has cards of other classes except neutral cards? Don't the developers think that such a design will cause great confusion? Maybe this can also be fixed. Sorry for saying some harsh words, but I really like this game and hope it can get better. I am an old card game player. In addition to Chinese card games, I have also played Slay the Spire, Duel Monsters, HearthStone, Gwent, Magic The Gathering, etc. in childhood. There has not been any eye-catching work in these years until the emergence of Deck of Souls. It is not perfect enough, but it has great potential. I very much hope that through repairs, optimizations and adjustments, this game can become excellent, and even comparable to Slay the Spire2 to be released next year. I really like the game Deck of Souls and hope that what I want to convey can be expressed clearly.

手残玩不了黑魂？那正好了，这款由Bigboot Studios研发的《魂之勇者》正是为致敬黑魂而做的硬核肉鸽卡牌爬塔类RPG，用卡牌爬塔的形式来体验一下另类的“魂式冒险”！ 游戏采用像素风格构筑了一个略带阴暗的地牢环境，各角色在此展开冒险角逐，虽说剧情并不是游戏的主题，但游戏起码是有着剧情的！这不比没有剧情一味的砍杀来的要香上许多么？ 游戏目前有着神圣骑士、圣洁巫妖和圣爪三个职业供我们挑选。不过后俩者需要解锁后才能使用，不同的职业有着不同的牌组和装备，这养成成分可比普通的卡牌爬塔游戏多了那么几分味道。 游戏主题还是卡牌爬塔，在大地图上选择路线后一往无前的前进，期间会有各种战斗、事件、商店、篝火等等场景等待触发。市面上常见的卡牌爬塔游戏的核心玩法基本都是卡牌与遗物的构筑BD，《魂之勇者》自然也少不了这种套路，只是还多了个装备的概念，在装备的加持下，让游戏的探索和养成更加有趣。 游戏在战斗的时候，每回合只能对一个敌人出手一次，如若是面对多个敌人，除了考虑手上的牌之外，还得考虑体力够不够，各种状态也让战斗变得更加扑朔迷离，而这也是游戏较为硬核的地方之一，让游戏多了些许策略性。当然，在遗物、装备和牌组构筑足够强力的情况下，所有的敌人都是小问题！（基本上遇不到这情况！） 游戏在中规中矩的卡牌爬塔游戏中添加了几分新颖的内容，无论是剧情的铺设还是装备的添加，到最后都是为卡牌战斗这么个核心机制服务，在单人对单牌的模式下更是让游戏多了那么几分硬核，整体而言算是一款相当优秀的硬核卡牌游戏了！ [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

[h1]《出牌吧！魂之勇者》简评[/h1] 像素美术风格、带有肉鸽元素、卡牌构筑对战游戏，《出牌吧！魂之勇者》这部作品在剧情、玩法以及爬塔模式上，都有自己的特色之处，虽然这些特色还存在着瑕疵，但也表现出不错的游戏性。游戏目前的体量不大，卡牌构筑策略欠缺了一些。但是游戏乐趣和制作质量还是很不错的。 很典型的类爬塔闯关模式，从开始房间，经历各类分支路线，最终进入到Boss房间，房间类型包括了战斗、精英战斗、Boss战斗、随机、灵魂之井等，玩家战斗胜利后，获得灵魂货币、新的卡牌，以及提升经验值升级角色获得新的装备/能力。该模式下，也有将角色扮演的一套练级养成体系融入其中，包括角色基础属性加点和升级后提升的装备/能力等内容，对于卡牌战斗的影响还是非常大的。 作为一款卡牌构筑对战游戏，其它的方面很大多数卡牌游戏类似，就是打出手牌，保证我方存活，击败所有敌人。不过，在《出牌吧！魂之勇者》之中，游戏机制对于出牌数量的限制进一步加强了，不再局限于消耗能量限制，还受限于敌人数量的限制——对方场上存活有几个怪物，玩家该回合便可以出几张牌。这个出牌机制很新颖，至少在卡牌游戏中见识过诸多出牌限制的规则，而本作的限制第一次见到，初开始游戏也确实有一种新鲜感。然而，本人对于卡牌构筑对战的体验，划分为三个阶段：初始有一定新鲜感-卡牌构筑体系欠缺-构筑策略有提升。之所以会有这般升降欺负的打牌感受，也正是受到此出牌受限的规则影响。 玩家开始阶段，该出牌机制所带来的弱点就有所表现，只不过这个时候卡牌数量较少，表现的不明显。但是随着战斗场次的增多，卡组新增卡牌也越来越多，其暴露出的问题就很明显了。 面对较少数量的敌人时，尤其是单个敌人，卡组之间的构筑体系，几乎是毫无意义，毕竟一回合只能出一张牌，完全就是单打独斗。面对复数以上数量的敌人，也确实可以提升提下打出卡牌之间的构筑关联性，但是也就是有所提升的程度。其次，卡组的体系构筑，问题也紧跟而来，有限的出牌数量，直接导致卡牌游戏中各种依靠抽牌、出牌来实现的卡组构筑流派，成为有牌无法打出的残废流派。反而是中毒、致残这种具有多回合时效性的负面影响流派更有效果。 不过，游戏中又引入了一套角色升级养成体系，角色战斗升级获得新的装备/能力，以及角色在灵魂之井中消耗灵魂货币提升五维属性。尤其是后者，力量、智力、体质、体力、机敏这五项属性点的加点，分别对角色的输出增幅、技能加成、承受伤害、能量提升、手牌数量等能力有很大的影响。再加上卡牌中还有“即时”、“放逐”、“冲刺”等词条之间的构筑，也确实能够在一定程度上缓解出牌限制的弊端，只是这个缓解其实是有限的，想要从量变到质变的大变化，很难。 此外，游戏中还有一个特色，那就是Boss战斗胜利后，有一个宽恕和处决的选择。宽恕，放敌人一条活路，但是作为自己背负命运的代价，需要从诸多负面惩罚中选择一条Debuff影响后续战斗。处决，就很简单，杀死敌人获得巨额的力量。虽然这还是一项卡牌机制，但是也和本作的剧情相关。根据剧情所简述的故事大体如下，玩家所扮演的主角，是一名身受重伤的勇者，其职责就是开启魔界传送门击败魔王，只不过看守传送门的将领们，深受魔界气息的污染，已经从身体到精神上都不正常了，甚至可以说魔物化。玩家击败他们之后，处决就是对其罪孽的审判并回复己身伤势，宽恕则是复活被击败的Boss但是会加重伤势。目前，只有前面三个章节的Boss——倒吊人、皇后和祭司，每个人为了守护自己的王国，有自己的理念，也有自己的遭遇，这一切的罪孽和苦痛，也都将由玩家去终结。（剧情世界观有些复杂，存在一定的宗教、神学、哲学的理念，需要细看。） [quote]关注[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url= https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

Game has a lot of potential. I really enjoy the story and gameplay. A few critiques though: - Really dislike how you can't take a card back once you place it. I really hope in the future you can either just drag it out or even have a full undo turn button (I would prefer the former, latter feels a bit cheaty to me). - I don't know if English is this developer's first language but I did notice some typos or grammatically incorrect sentences, but everything is still perfectly readable and understandable. - Game doesn't really explain mechanics that well, this isn't a huge bother for me but I could see it being annoying for other players. - I wish you could right click cards and get a full breakdown even though a lot of the stuff is visual already or that you can already hover for the most important info. It would hopefully include card type, keyword descriptions, allow you to see the cards it generates (if applicable), all that good stuff. - Lack of variety. This is an EA game, I do not care about this right now but as the game develops I hope that this will improve, but this doesn't bother me at all. - The third character sucks ass. No other way to say it. Smoke bomb costing 6 stamina is way too much to get any value from him. Maybe I'm just playing the character wrong and my brain isn't big enough but I've literally lost to the second battle because of how poorly he plays. He needs the biggest improvements imo besides the card to hand feature as mentioned above. - I would really like to see a Loadout system for the characters to generate different starting cards rather than it be randomized, and have rewards tied to winning with those specific loadouts. Similar to something found in SpellRogue. - Game is in EA so again, this isn't a huge deal for me right now but there definitely needs to be some polish for animations and things made clearer for when specific abilities are triggering at what time. It's not super confusing but definitely could be improved. Deck of Souls is a well crafted EA game that brings uniqueness to the genre that I haven't seen before. The fact that you can adapt your characters in almost any way you like (although some are obviously harder than others), is a really fun and enjoyable mechanic. Game has a TON of potential and for an EA title I'd say there's enough content here to justify the $11. Really looking forward to seeing how this game develops!

[h1]简介[/h1] 《出牌吧！魂之勇者》作为一款肉鸽爬塔卡牌对战游戏，现阶段一共上线了3个职业，初始职业是手拿大棒的骑士。对没看错，就是骑士，因为就算我给他换了一把长剑，也只是让大棒变成剑的颜色，外观还是大棒。游戏是非常常规的卡牌游戏，玩法和卡牌的构筑方面与其他同类游戏也没太大的区别。可能是一次玩在Boss战居然是连战，我直接被一套带走。 [h1]构筑有点费劲[/h1] 作为一款卡牌游戏，本作与其他同类型的卡牌爬塔游戏大差不差，只是在卡牌机制方面，制作组有着自己的想法和理解。首先，本作去掉了那种能一轮打出n多卡牌造成大量伤害的玩法，出牌是有牌位的，一个怪物只能挂一个牌，并且出牌需要消耗体力。如果怪物多又没有AOE卡牌，总会有1到2个小怪成为伤害的漏网之鱼。不过，道具牌和魔法牌不受这类限制，但这类牌的获取要靠运气和道具店，也就是说即使你有卡牌，如果没有体力出牌，也只能罚站硬扛一轮。老实说，基于我对这类游戏的玩法和理解，我不太清楚这样设计的原理和原因。虽然在爬塔的过程中，商店、休息点、装备点等设置挺多，但要让BD成型还是差得太多。这种限制太影响游戏体验了，能否出个无限模式或者复古模式？ [h1]升级和卡牌的联动[/h1] 可能是为了中和我之前提到的卡牌卡手情况，本作有一套装备和升级加点系统，装备上还能克制技能，增加生存或攻击能力。在爬塔过程中，赢得卡牌对战也能获得货币，除了购买道具外，还能在休息点进行升级。升级的5个属性也是常见RPG的维度，前期我通常把点数投入到体力和血量上，以应对体力紧张的情况。但实际战斗下来，这些并没办法弥补整体战斗节奏的缺失。因为战斗中的怪物是随机的，遇到较多的怪物会带来一些策略性和爽感，而单个小怪或BOSS则有些让人感到乏味。 [h1]介斯嘛[/h1] 游戏的核心卡牌战斗玩法看似做了很多的减法，但却需要用一个框架将这些剑法框起来。具体的描述可以参考上面，总感觉这套战斗系统是两个不同的人做的，因为割裂感非常强烈。卡牌构筑是一套玩法，时机使用又是一套玩法，两者之间没有任何过渡或连接。简单总结就是你组你的，我打我的。 [h1]总结[/h1] 总的来说《出牌吧！魂之勇者》还是有一些特色的，比如boss战结束的审判，是宽恕还是处死。还有就是卡牌的异常属性词条（debuff）的加入，但这些都无法维持住游戏的基本盘--好玩。 [quote]关注鉴赏组：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45134494]浮生评测[/url] ←"浮生若梦，一鉴倾心，邀您共赏人间烟火" 加入Steam组：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/LLFLLFF]浮生评测[/url]←“一起追寻'浮生若梦'般的游戏体验” 开始“浮生若梦”鉴赏组的奇幻之旅！[/quote]

A solid turn based roguelike with a deck building system. There are 3 classes, each with their own cards and playstyles. One big difference between this game and others is that you can normally only play 1 card per enemy unit, however you can bypass this is cards have traits such as "instant" which plays them immediately, or "redeem" which plays them when they are discarded so ideally you are able to play a bunch of cards that trigger off each other. There is also a gear system, you can buy/loot gear from ships and events and there is even set bonuses, as well as being able to upgrade/enchant gear. There is also some meta progression although the currency you earn for it is pretty slow to earn so you'll want to focus on a few key upgrades such as getting a free revive or starting off with an extra piece of gear. I'd say my one complaint with the game right now is that you cannot pick your starting deck for a hero, it's randomized. So if you want to play a particular deck you need to start and abandon games over and over until it pops up which is annoying. Hopefully the devs change this in the future. But all in all the game is fun, I got it as part of a game bundle so for a decent discount and enjoyed my time with it.

来自中文社区玩家想给游戏设计者的反馈，希望你们能看到（后面会有机器翻译）：首先游戏本身的机制设计很巧妙，虽然有些玩家说卡手（即出牌感觉并不流畅），不过那应该是没有理解卡牌的设计机制，以巫妖来举例，即时（instant）、冲刺（rush）、必出（redeem）、电链（zap）、智慧（wise）的牌组之间互相可以构成不同的连击卡组构筑，这是非常值得称赞的，显著区别于rougelike类牌组构筑游戏。但问题也随之而来，本人玩了十几局巫妖的游戏，可以说体验非常糟糕，普通难度通关问题不大，因为无论用什么套路似乎都可以碾压过去，但通关之后解锁更多牌组后反而出现了问题，巫妖的牌组核心应该是即时的卡牌基础配合zap流派的“自动出牌（autoplay）”或redeem流派的弃牌触发卡牌效果，但由此而来的问题是这一系列套路在面对有自动反击的怪物时，往往因为反击的伤害把自己杀死，甚至是无法避免的问题，而刻意规避autoplay或弃牌产生的自动伤害则会发生根本打不过去从而因为时间流逝慢性自杀的死循环。而自动反击的怪物，除了第二关的关底BOSS以外，第四关的常规战斗可以说遍地都是，根本无法回避这个问题，导致巫妖这一职业的游戏体验非常糟糕，而解决的办法似乎只有祈祷能够出现攻击回血的被动或叠加护甲的装备，这一设计理念绝对是会给玩家造成极大挫败的失败设计，因为你不能指望一个游戏的通关与否，需要建立在“必须具备的唯一运气”，这会使这个游戏让玩家认为“存在重大设计缺陷”。另外智慧（wise）的设计也有问题，当前的设计是只有当wise类的牌出现在手牌时，有zap类的牌添加新的牌才能减少wise的需求，这会导致wise类的牌在实际操作中根本没有操作空间，你只能祈祷这些牌恰好可以同时出现在自己的手牌，否则wise的牌就是废物。如果改为“在卡牌池中添加新牌即可生效”，那么可以极大提升这一流派的自由度。还有一张传奇级别的卡牌dragon breath，本身需要10次rush才能免费打出，而这张卡牌是会出现在开局设置的自动获得传奇卡牌中，这会导致巫妖在前期根本没有办法打出这张牌，无论是满足10层rush还是直接打出的12点能量，从而让这张牌成为废牌，只能在中立传奇卡牌wish产生的免费选择中才有用武之地，那么这张卡牌的设计就是不成功的；我认为可以添加必出“redeem”，让这张卡拍可以和redeem流派产生配合，这样才能体现出“传奇”的设计效果。另外还有一些中文评论中提到的“中毒poison”层数问题，这其实是翻译问题，中文的翻译把原来的意思完全弄反了，这原本是游戏设计非常独到的地方，因为中毒本来就应该是随着时间的流逝越来越严重（get worse），但中文翻译却变成了会每回合减少中毒的程度，导致游戏评价在中文社区很不理想，希望可以更改文本说明 Subject: Feedback from a Chinese Community Player for the Game Designers (Machine Translation Follows): First, the core mechanics of the game itself are very clever. Although some players complain about feeling "stuck" (meaning card play doesn't feel smooth), that's likely due to not fully understanding the card design mechanics. Taking the Lich as an example, the interactions between decks built around instant, rush, redeem, zap, and wise cards allow for various combo-focused deck constructions. This is highly commendable and significantly different from other roguelike deck-building games. However, problems arise from this. I've played over ten games with the Lich, and I must say the experience was very poor. Clearing the normal difficulty isn't a big issue, as almost any strategy seems to steamroll through it. But the problems start after unlocking more decks upon clearing the game. The Lich's deck core should be based on instant cards combined with either the zap archetype's "autoplay" or the redeem archetype's discard-trigger effects. The resulting problem is that these strategies often lead to the player killing themselves against monsters with automatic counterattacks. This seems unavoidable. Conversely, deliberately avoiding autoplay or the self-damage from discarding creates a different death loop: you simply can't deal enough damage fast enough, leading to a slow death from the turn timer. Monsters with automatic counterattacks are practically everywhere in the regular battles of Act 4, not just the Act 2 final boss. This makes the problem completely unavoidable, resulting in a very poor gameplay experience for the Lich class. The only apparent solutions seem to be praying to find passives that heal on attack or equipment that stacks armor. This design philosophy is absolutely a failure that creates immense player frustration. You cannot expect the success or failure of clearing the game to depend solely on "obtaining the one necessary piece of luck." This will make players perceive the game as having "major design flaws." Additionally, the wise design has issues. The current mechanic is that the requirement for a wise card is only reduced when a zap card adds a new card while that wise card is already in your hand. This makes wise cards practically unusable in actual gameplay. You can only hope these specific cards coincidentally appear in your hand together; otherwise, wise cards are useless. Changing it to "take effect when new cards are added to the draw pile" would significantly increase the freedom and viability of this archetype. There's also a Legendary card, dragon breath, which requires 10 stacks of rush to play for free. This card can appear in the automatically granted Legendary cards at the start of a run. This makes it impossible for the Lich to play this card in the early game, whether by meeting the 10 rush requirement or paying its 12 Energy cost. Consequently, the card becomes dead weight, only useful if obtained for free via the neutral Legendary card wish. Therefore, the design of this card is unsuccessful. I suggest adding the redeem keyword to it, allowing it to synergize with redeem strategies. Only then would it truly feel "Legendary." Finally, regarding the "poison" stack issue mentioned in some Chinese reviews: this is actually a translation problem. The Chinese translation completely reversed the original meaning. This was originally a very unique design point in the game, as poison should logically get worse over time. However, the Chinese translation stated that the poison effect decreases each turn, leading to poor reviews in the Chinese community. Please correct the text description.

Honestly, I'd really love to recommend this game... but I just can't, and it's really a shame. Fundamentally, this game proposes to offer a lot of fun and interesting mechanics. It's also generally very fun to play. That said, it's also clearly an unfinished work that the developer has grown tired of and abandoned, and that's really a shame because the foundation here is just so promising. Even fundamental card systems associated with the default decks of one of the three characters is just straight up broken and does not work as described (or in any sensible way at all). This bug would be honestly impossible to miss in any testing (it's an issue that occurs in nearly every combat encounter) and has been widely reported for years as far as I can tell. There are other, sometimes more subtle, indications of this being an unfinished project the more time you spend with it. Mechanics aren't explained (and some that are explained don't behave as claimed), choices are confusing, gameplay balance is all over the place, and the objectives and story are oddly unclear (this last part hearkens to the soulslike portions of the game's DNA, perhaps, but the protagonist characters clearly have a ton of history and backstory that is simply unavailable to the player). Alongside these cons is a game that, for bursts of time, is really honestly very fun and compelling to play. This review is not being left by someone who is angry at the game, it's just coming from the perspective of someone who sees how much fun this game could be and is sorely disappointed by how little additional effort it would seem to take to get that game to the level of polish and presentation necessary to call it a finished product.

Deck of Souls, developed by Bigboot Studios and published by HeroCraft PC, is a dark fantasy roguelike deckbuilder that attempts to blend methodical, Souls-inspired design with strategic card-based combat. It places players in a grim, looping world where death is not failure but a necessary step toward growth, and every encounter demands careful planning rather than quick reactions. The game distinguishes itself by translating concepts like stamina management, equipment burden, and deliberate pacing into a turn-based system, creating an experience that feels slower and more calculated than most titles in the genre. Combat is built around a deck of cards representing attacks, defensive maneuvers, and special abilities. Each action consumes a limited resource similar to stamina, which does not fully reset between turns. This creates a constant need to manage resources over multiple rounds, forcing players to think ahead and avoid overcommitting. Unlike more fluid deckbuilders that encourage chaining multiple cards in a single turn, this system rewards restraint and precision. Every decision carries weight, and a poorly timed action can leave the player exposed during critical moments. Progression is closely tied to the game’s roguelike structure, where each run offers a chance to gather new resources, unlock additional cards, and refine strategies. Defeated enemies yield souls that can be converted into new abilities, gradually expanding the player’s options. Over time, this creates a sense of growth that persists across runs, even as individual attempts may end in failure. The system encourages experimentation, as players can try different combinations of cards and abilities to discover effective strategies. Character variety adds depth to the experience, with multiple classes offering distinct approaches to combat. Each class has access to unique cards and mechanics, allowing players to tailor their playstyle. Some builds emphasize direct damage and straightforward tactics, while others rely on status effects or more intricate interactions between cards. This flexibility enhances replayability, as different combinations can lead to significantly different experiences. Despite its strengths, the game’s deliberate pacing can be both a defining feature and a potential drawback. The stamina system, while thematically consistent, can slow combat to a point where encounters feel drawn out. Combined with the randomness inherent in deckbuilding, this can lead to situations where progress feels limited by luck rather than skill. Early runs in particular may feel restrictive, as players have fewer tools available and must rely heavily on basic mechanics. The roguelike structure introduces variety through randomized encounters and rewards, but it also contributes to inconsistency. Some runs may offer strong synergies and clear paths to success, while others can feel significantly more challenging due to less favorable conditions. This unpredictability is part of the genre’s appeal, but it can also create moments of frustration, especially when combined with the game’s slower pace. Visually, Deck of Souls adopts a dark and moody aesthetic that aligns well with its themes. The environments and character designs emphasize a sense of decay and danger, reinforcing the atmosphere of a world trapped in a cycle of death and rebirth. While the graphics are not particularly advanced, they are effective in conveying the tone and maintaining clarity during gameplay. The audio design complements this with subdued music and sound effects that enhance the tension without becoming distracting. The narrative provides a framework for the gameplay, exploring themes of repetition, survival, and power. While it does not take center stage, it adds context to the player’s actions and helps tie the mechanics together. The idea of progressing through repeated cycles of death gives meaning to the roguelike structure, making each attempt feel like part of a larger journey rather than a disconnected experience. There are areas where the game could benefit from further refinement. Balance issues, particularly in the early stages, can make the experience feel uneven, and certain systems may not be as polished as they could be. The interface and overall presentation are functional but lack the level of refinement seen in more established titles. These elements do not detract entirely from the experience, but they highlight the game’s rough edges. Overall, Deck of Souls is a bold and thoughtful take on the deckbuilding genre that introduces a more deliberate and strategic approach to combat. Its combination of Souls-like mechanics and card-based gameplay creates a unique identity, even if the execution is not always consistent. For players who enjoy slower, more methodical experiences and are willing to adapt to its pacing, it offers a rewarding and distinctive challenge. Rating: 8/10

As much as I want to like it I must admit: I have seen much more polished game with much worse review score. Perhaps it is a psychological need to excuse a game that would otherwise turn out great, if it was properly finished, that is. Game tips and descriptions in-game are basically non-existent. Half of the time I am not sure if a card effect is broken and nothing happens, the card is discarded or burnt. Maybe it works, effects are just so mellow, I don't register properly. Burning overflowing cards in hand is a bad taste in my opinion - you either discard cards over the limit at the end of turn, don't draw at all or burn the freshly drawn card. There is a reason basically all other good card games do one of the three. It's especially grating when I am playing as a lich where cards often times autocast, but the effects are so meh I sometimes can't tell whether I have burnt a card or it was played. This is probably a personal issue, but I am not a fan of the combined art style - it feels like a mesh of assets: pixel sprites, UI elements, portraits, video elements... it feels like belonging to separate games. Animations are probably taking too much time for a looper game. Sprites are lovely though. As someone pointed out - the core original mechanic this game has is also its biggest drawback. You play cards by assigning them to individual mobs meaning if there are three enemies, you can play a three standard cards a turn. If there is but one enemy (which holds true for most boss fights), you can play only one card. This is offset by introduction of the instant keyword which allows to play a card immediately from hand forgoing the limitation. Problem is - you want most of your cards to be instants, because you will not be able to outmatch enemies otherwise, the resource economy would be stacked against you as the enemies will eventually mount more damage than you'd be able to mitigate/heal/block in a given time. This forces you to always pursue certain card choices, which severely limits the deckbuilding options. In the end to core original mechanic is something you try to go around during you gameplay. Is that a good mechanic then? I am not sure, however the execution here seems to be lacking as it seems that placement/order does not really matter as all cards seem to be resolved simultaneously - yours first, then enemies, so it makes no sense to block a particular enemy or use a free window for another enemy to launch an attack. Or perhaps it's just that unfinished. Most cards and mechanics are uninspired tbh. Knight is very straightforward, Ninja is clunky due to stealth bomb cards being so damn expensive (or rather - he is clunky for half of the game and after I get certain cards it becomes trivial), the only saving grace is the lich dude who represent quite an inspired symbiosis of flavor and mechanics with his shtick being time magic even though it still leaves something to be desired. What would turn this game into a recommendation? Get the art/UI sorted out and unified. Create proper in-game tooltips and descriptions. Bug test properly. Tight up the core card mechanic for order/placement to matter. Make the card effects a bit more crispy and nuanced for the sake of distinguishment of what is happening on board. Scrap the card-burn mechanic for a more approachable solution.

Preface this by saying that I do like this game and enjoy it but I do have low standards. Poor programming of the card game itself, there are steps that are out of order and cards execute themselves in ways that make no sense for their stated wording or most CCG style games. Story is ok, if nothing new but the actual writing itself feels machine translated. There are archaic uses of words and other strange phrases used throughout the game. Menu design is bland with generic tinted boxes and plain white text that gives it an unpolished feel. Pick it up on sale, its fun.

The unique card system makes each game unpredictable and exciting. Deck of Souls immerses you in a world full of intrigue.
The game appeals to beginners and experienced players alike. The ease of learning and depth of gameplay make it versatile.
The balancing of maps and characters in Deck of Souls is quite good, making the game always fresh and relevant.
